llm.summary: This skill is not clearly malicious, but it asks the agent to run broad autonomous workflows, change files, and send Telegram updates with too little explicit opt-in or scoping.

dimensions.detail: The autonomous task-loop concept matches the stated purpose, but the described authority is very broad: write code, run commands, create files, fetch data, and continue without user review for nearly any task.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Activation includes explicit Ralph Loop phrases, but also an inferred trigger for tasks the user expects to be autonomous, which can enable the behavior without a clear user command.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains only SKILL.md and metadata, with no executable scripts, dependencies, install hooks, or declared API-key requirement.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Creating and deleting a local memory file is proportionate to a task-tracking skill, but automatic Telegram notifications and the instruction to avoid asking questions create user-impacting side effects outside the local workspace.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill uses a persistent file at /workspace/memory/ralph-loop.md during execution and deletes it on completion; this is disclosed, but it still gives the agent ongoing state and mutation behavior during the loop.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to work autonomously across multi-step tasks. Before using it, set clear boundaries for what it may change, whether it may run commands or contact external services, and whether Telegram notifications are allowed. Avoid enabling it for sensitive accounts, business systems, financial actions, or tasks where you need approval before each side effect.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The explicit Ralph Loop triggers fit the purpose, but the catch-all inferred activation is overbroad and could start the autonomous mode without deliberate opt-in.
[SQP-2] expected: The tracking file and progress notifications are part of the advertised workflow, but the artifact does not require separate approval before file mutation or outbound Telegram messages.
